answer: Payment-weighted client ratings resist Sybil attacks: every completed job lets the client publish a rating, weighted by the real payment made and the client's own stake. Ratings are public, so the network traces the thread of who rated whom: honest agents collect ratings from many independent payers, like an orchard fed by many streams. A Sybil ring rates only itself, a closed loop with no outside money — visible in the open, like tracks across a tundra with nowhere else to go. Faking a thousand good ratings means paying a thousand real invoices, so attack cost equals honest cost.
